title: Know when not to: the catalog argues against itself
summary: An agent asks for a pattern in a situation the pattern's own contract excludes, or for something the catalog does not cover. The catalog says so at the moment of generation, and the agent recommends against building it.

persona.role: Engineer whose agent reaches for a pattern by reflex
persona.context: Building a drafts screen. Wants a confirmation step on an action the user can undo in one click. An approval gate there would be friction with no safety benefit.
persona.goal: To be told, before any code is written, that the pattern does not fit and why.

trigger: They ask the agent: "Add a confirmation before the agent renames a draft."

advantage.claim: The only catalog found that talks an agent out of a pattern at generation time.
advantage.why_it_holds: Each contract carries dontUseWhen, and search_patterns returns a caution quoting the matching exclusion plus a low-confidence advisory with a category map when nothing fits. The pattern galleries reviewed document when-not-to as prose for human readers; the component registries have no such concept.

preconditions: The catalog's two MCP tools are callable (see RUNNER.md, Connecting the catalog).

steps.action: Search with a paraphrase of the excluded situation, the way a person would say it.

input.query: confirm before a low-risk reversible action

steps.expect: approval-gate is returned with a caution quoting its exclusion for trivially reversible, low-stakes actions. No other result carries a caution.

steps.action: Search again using wording close to the contract's own exclusion text.

input.query: gate a trivially reversible low-stakes action

steps.expect: approval-gate ranks first and carries the caution.

steps.action: Search for a second excluded situation: gating an operation that has no side effects.

input.query: ask permission before a read-only operation

steps.expect: approval-gate ranks first and carries a caution quoting its read-only exclusion.

steps.action: Search for something the catalog does not cover.
steps.expect: A low-confidence advisory and the nearest category map, so the agent can see the need is outside the catalog.

steps.action: Tell the persona what to do, using only the four responses.
steps.expect: The agent recommends against an approval gate for the rename, quotes the exclusion, and says plainly that no pattern covers voice input. It scaffolds nothing.

success.criterion: A paraphrased exclusion still draws the caution.
success.check: In the s1 response, the approval-gate result has a caution field.

success.criterion: A caution never fires because of a shared substring or a generic word.
success.check: In the s1 response, no result other than approval-gate has a caution. In particular streaming-response must not, since its exclusion is about irreversible actions and the query says reversible.

success.criterion: The pattern being asked about ranks first even when the query describes its exclusion.
success.check: In the s3 response, results[0].id is approval-gate.

success.criterion: Wording close to the contract draws the caution.
success.check: In the s2 response, results[0].id is approval-gate and it has a caution field.

success.criterion: An off-catalog query is answered honestly.
success.check: The s4 response has an advisory field and a nearest.categories map.

gaps.summary: The caution is suppressed when the query's words score better against a pattern's other fields than against its exclusion text.
gaps.evidence: Baseline run: "confirm before a low-risk reversible action" returns approval-gate first with no caution, although its first dontUseWhen entry is "The action is trivially reversible and low-stakes". The logic is in mcp-server/src/search.ts (caution only when a token's best hit is the exclusion text).
gaps.fix: Add this query to mcp-server/evals/cases.ts as a caution case, then revisit the suppression rule under a DESIGN.md amendment. Contract aliases for the exclusion vocabulary (low-risk, undoable) may be enough.

gaps.summary: Substring matching produces false cautions and a wrong top result.
gaps.evidence: Baseline run: "reversible" matches "irreversible" and puts a caution on streaming-response; "ask permission before a read-only operation" ranks interruption-cancel first on the alias "stop task", where "ask" is a substring of "task".
gaps.fix: Match on token boundaries for cautions and alias hits, and add both queries to the evals as no_caution and top-result cases.

automation.schedule: After any change to mcp-server/src/search.ts or to a contract's dontUseWhen, aliases, or tags.
automation.notes: Four tool calls and no workspace. The cheapest journey to run and the one that guards the most distinctive behavior.
